traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 10 Annonaceae: trees, shrubs or climbers with aromatic wood and leaves; leaves alternate, entire; no stipules; sepals usually 3; petals often 6 in two whorls of 3; stamens numerous, spirally set; carpels numerous or few, free, rarely joined into one ovary, each often stalked in fruit, dry or fleshy (the custard apple's fused into one fleshy mass): read as an aggregate fruit, sometimes a berry. Simple leaves from 'entire' (inferred).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 198, family Annonaceae: phyllotaxis pattern distichous, usually; read as {"distichous": "usually"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 198, family Annonaceae: inflorescence solitary or cyme; read as {"cyme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.petal_whorls.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 10 Annonaceae: "sepals usually 3; petals often 6 in two whorls of 3".

traits.stamen_form.note: Flora of China vol. 19, Annonaceae (family account, eFloras taxon 10047, read 2026-10-18): stamens many, spirally arranged, with a short stout filament and a connective broadened and flat-topped over the anther: a flat strap with its pollen sacs along most of its length, read as laminar.

traits.floral_receptacle.note: Flora of China vol. 19, Annonaceae (family account, read 2026-10-18): receptacle enlarged, flat to raised under the spiral stamens and carpels; read as convex (a low dome, not a torus).
